newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia sends war crimes suspect to Hague tribunal.
newsitem.headline: Croatia sends war crimes suspect to Hague tribunal.

text.p: Croatia said on Monday it had extradited a Croat wanted by the international War Crimes Tribunal in The Hague, days after Western pressure piled on the Balkan country to comply with the court.

Zlatko Aleksovski, 36, was indicted for atrocities against Moslem civilians during the Bosnian war. He was arrested in Croatia almost a year ago but authorities had not sent him to the Hague, claiming he was ill.
"Legal conditions for Aleksovski's extradition have been met and...he was handed over to The Hague," a government statement carried by the state news agency HINA said.

Last month the United States conveyed its dismay with Croatia's failure to cooperate with the U.N. war-crimes tribunal by abstaining from an International Monetary Fund vote to approve nearly $500 million in loans to the former Yugoslav republic.
One diplomat said Croatia was under "serious pressure" to extradite Aleksovski, a Bosnian Croat. Doctors sent by the Tribunal examined him last week and pronounced him fit to travel, diplomats said.
Another Bosnian Croat war crimes suspect handed himself voluntarily to the Tribunal in April last year, but has not been tried yet.
